\[
C_s = \operatorname{bilateral}^{k}(C),
\quad
M = \operatorname{med}_{5 \times 5}\left(\operatorname{round}(Y)\right),
\quad
C' = \begin{cases} 0 & M < \operatorname{mean}_{s \times s}(M) - d \\ C_s & \text{otherwise} \end{cases},
\qquad k = 2,\ s = 9,\ d = 4
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(C_s\): The smoothed color
- \(M\): The median filtered luma
- \(k, s, d\): The passes, the line window and the line threshold

The colors are smoothed by k passes of the bilateral filter of Tomasi and Manduchi in color mode, which flattens areas while keeping edges. The lines come from the luma Y, rounded to whole levels and median filtered over 5 by 5 to remove noise. A pixel is a line where this median is darker than its local mean over s by s by more than d, the rule of the adaptive mean threshold. Lines are black, and all other pixels take the smoothed color. The recipe is PixelNexus's own.
